items.title: Scattering data of the central model class: the scattering motion, the impact parameter, the asymptotic directions, the deflection conventions and the uniform-incident preparation
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the preparation and cross-section measures.

This item fixes the **scattering data** of the restricted model class of
[[post-cm05-central-model]] and the preparation conventions in which the
scattering statements of this page are phrased. All objects are model data;
nothing here is a measured value.

**(i) The scattering model.** A **central scattering model** is a model of
class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with $N=2$ labels, masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), no external forces, and a
static central pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])
whose collision-excluded interval satisfies $(0,\infty)\subseteq J_0$, so
that the only forbidden configuration is the collision $r=0$. Its **reduced
problem** is the one-label problem of class (ii) with reduced mass
$\mu:=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$ ([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\mu]=\mu$) and the same
potential, presented through the relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$; by
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] the relative coordinate of every motion of
the model is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ and every pair of an
affine centre-of-mass motion and a solution of the reduced equation on a
common interval reconstructs a motion of the model.

**(ii) Scattering motions and their data.** Let $r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$
be a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$
with values $|r(t)|\in J_0$ and with constant angular momentum
$j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ for $J>0$ and an oriented orthonormal triad
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]],
[[lem-cm-oriented-orthonormal-triads]]). Call $r$ a **scattering motion** when it has a unique apsis $t_*$ with $\rho=|r|$ decreasing strictly before $t_*$, increasing strictly after it, $\rho(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$, and the nonzero limits below exist with the stated speed, equal finite impact-distance limits and finite equal half-advances. These are defining conditions, not deductions for arbitrary $C^2$ potentials. The finite-range theorem requires $u=0$ beyond some $R$, $E,J>0$, a simple outer turning point $V(r_*)=E$, $V'(r_*)<0$, $V(r)<E$ for $r>r_*$, and a trajectory staying above and attaining $r_*$. The repulsive Coulomb theorem instead requires $u=\kappa/\rho$, $\kappa,E,J>0$ and a trajectory attaining its turning radius. Each theorem proves the defining conditions in its own scope. Its **energy** is the constant
$$E:=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert r\rvert)>0$$
of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] (constant by
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4), its **asymptotic
velocities** are the limits
$$v_-:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}r'(t),\qquad v_+:=\lim_{t\to+\infty}r'(t),$$
taken in the sense of [[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]
(their existence under the hypotheses is a theorem, not a convention), and
its **scattering speed** is
$$v_\infty:=\lVert v_-\rVert_2=\lVert v_+\rVert_2=\sqrt{2E/\mu},$$
the equality being part of the scattering theorems. The **incoming branch**
is the trajectory restricted to times before its apsis. The **impact parameter** is the asymptotic perpendicular-distance limit
$$b:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_-\rVert_2}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2}=\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_+\rVert_2}{\lVert v_+\rVert_2}=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}>0.$$
Here the distance at each time is to the line through the origin in the limiting velocity direction, not to an exact affine trajectory line. For a finite-range potential, the sufficiently early incoming tail is a straight half-line whose affine extension has this distance; for Coulomb these are only limits, with no exact free tail or finite longitudinal intercept claimed. The dimension is $[b]=\ell$.

**(iii) Polar advance and deflection conventions.** Fix polar data
$(\rho,\theta)$ of the scattering motion in the triad, $r=\rho\,n(\theta)$,
$n(\varphi):=\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\varphi\,e_2$
([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]), and let $t_*$ be an apsis time,
$|r(t_*)|=\min_t|r(t)|$. The **polar advance of one half** is
$$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty),$$
defined by the limits asserted in the scattering theorems, and the
**polar advance of the motion** is $2\Delta$. The **scattering angle** is the
undirected angle between the asymptotic velocity directions,
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2\,\lVert v_+\rVert_2}\right)\in[0,\pi],$$
the incoming and outgoing velocity directions are oriented, so this is not the smaller unoriented angle between two lines;
the **signed velocity rotation** is the continuous rotation angle of
$r'(t)$, measured counterclockwise about $e_3$ relative to the incoming
direction, so that a positive value is a counterclockwise turn. The scattering
theorems give $\cos\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta)$ and the signed
rotation $2\Delta-\pi$; in particular, when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ the scattering
angle is
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi),$$
while outside that range $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the wrapped value $\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$.
The **deflection map** at fixed model potential $u$, reduced mass $\mu$ and energy $E>0$ is the partial map $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)$ on those $b>0$ for which a scattering motion exists and all such motions have the same angle. Its corresponding angular momentum magnitude varies as
$$J(b)=\mu b v_\infty=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b.$$
Time translation and rotation of a motion do not change its angle. **Deflection branches** are $C^1$ branches of this partial map as defined in [[def-cm-scattering-data]].

**(iv) The uniform-incident preparation (adopted model datum).** The
**uniform-incident preparation** of a central scattering model with cutoff
$b_{\max}>0$ and flux $\Phi>0$ is the following adopted model of a scattering
experiment for the reduced problem: independent incident reduced labels with common energy $E>0$ and impact-azimuth probability measure
$$P(A)=\frac{\nu(A\cap D_{\max})}{\pi b_{\max}^2},\qquad D_{\max}=(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi).$$
Its density is $b/(\pi b_{\max}^2)$, and its total mass is one since $\nu(D_{\max})=\pi b_{\max}^2$. Angular momentum magnitude is $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$; its plane orientation may vary with azimuth. The **incident flux** $\Phi$ is the expected number of incident labels per unit area per unit time, with $[\Phi]=\ell^{-2}\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). The adopted total arrival rate is $\Phi\pi b_{\max}^2$, so for a Borel set $A\subseteq D_{\max}$ the expected incident rate is
$$\dot N(A)=\Phi\pi b_{\max}^2 P(A)=\Phi\nu(A).$$
Here $\nu$ is the incident area measure of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]. For a
specified deflection branch $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ and a
Borel scattering-angle window $Y\subseteq(\theta_1,\theta_2)$, the predicted
rate from that branch under this cutoff preparation is
$$\dot N_{\mathrm{br}}(Y):=\Phi\,\nu\!\left(\left\{(b,\varphi)\in D_{\max}:a_1<b<a_2,\ \theta(b)\in Y\right\}\right).$$
The preimage is Borel because $\theta$ is continuous on its branch. For a
finite family of branches with pairwise disjoint incident intervals, branch
rates add, including when their angular images overlap. Incidences outside
recorded scattering branches are not assigned an outgoing scattering angle
by this definition. The rate above integrates over the full impact-azimuth
range; it is a model prediction, not a detected count. Comparing it with data
requires a separately specified experiment, apparatus model, sampling model
and statistical analysis.

**(v) Reading conventions.** All angles and lengths above are data of the
**relative** problem: angles are computed from the relative coordinate
$r=x_1-x_2$ and its asymptotic velocities $v_\pm$, not from either label's
trajectory. The centre of mass $X$ and the reconstruction formulas
$x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and $x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$, with $M=m_1+m_2$, are
those of clause (i), [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]] and
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4. They show that individual-label
directions generally differ from the relative direction and from each
other. "Target", "projectile" and "detector" are names for model components
and carry no empirical claim.

**(vi) Exclusions and status.** The class excludes velocity- or
time-dependent, non-central and non-potential forces; constraints and
reaction forces; collisions $r=0$; external forces; and models with more than
two labels, exactly as in [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (v). The
preparation of clause (iv) is one adopted idealisation among many; the
scattering theorems state separately which potentials, energies and angular
momenta produce the data of clauses (ii)-(iii). The quantities $\mu$, $u$
(with any parameters it carries), $E$, $J$, $b$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model
data; quantitative empirical use requires separately stated measured inputs
with uncertainties, and no statement of this page asserts that any physical
system is exactly a central scattering model or that any beam is exactly
uniform.

**Why the objects are defined.** The relative coordinate is a central-force
trajectory by the cited reduction theorem; the attached energy and angular
momentum are defined by [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] and are constant
on the trajectory by [[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4 and
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]]; the impact parameter is defined by its limiting distance, with existence and equality proved under the theorem-specific hypotheses; and the
preparation measure of clause (iv) is the measure $\nu$ of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. The arccosine of clause (iii) is defined because
the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives
$|\langle v_-,v_+\rangle|/(\lVert v_-\rVert_2\lVert v_+\rVert_2)\le1$
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]).

**Mathematical status.** The vocabulary is attached to the adopted model
class of [[post-cm05-central-model]]; the existence of the limits, the
identities for $v_\infty$, $b$, $\Delta$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$, and the
form of the deflection map under explicit potential hypotheses are the
content of the mathematics and physics theorems of this page, not of this
definition.

items.title: The differential and truncated total cross-sections of a deflection branch: densities, units, branch sums and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Borel measures.

This item fixes the **cross-section** vocabulary of the central scattering
models of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] relative to the uniform-incident
preparation of that definition.

**(i) The differential cross-section of a branch.** Let a central scattering
model be given, let $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a **deflection branch**
in the sense of [[def-cm-scattering-data]] — an interval $(a_1,a_2)$ of
impact parameters with $\theta$ of class $C^1$ and $\theta'(b)\ne0$ — and
suppose the branch **records the deflection** of the model: for every
$b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of the model with impact parameter $b$,
fixed energy $E$ and angular momentum magnitude $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$ has scattering angle
$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\theta(b)$. Write
$(a_1,a_2)\ni b\mapsto\theta\in(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ for this bijection and
$b(\theta):=\theta^{-1}(\theta)$ for its inverse
([[def-cm-scattering-data]]). The **differential cross-section of the
branch** is the function
$$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta):=\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'\bigl(b(\theta)\bigr)\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2),$$
the cross-section density of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]. Its dimension is
$[\mathrm d\sigma/\mathrm d\Omega]=\ell^2$ (solid angle dimensionless in the
chosen convention, [[def-cm01-units]]), and one says "per steradian" for the
unit of solid angle.

**(ii) Branch sums.** Let $\mathcal B=\{(a_1^{(j)},a_2^{(j)},\theta_j)\}_{j=1}^N$
be a finite family of deflection branches of the same model whose incident
intervals $(a_1^{(j)},a_2^{(j)})$ are pairwise disjoint, with each branch
recording the model's deflections as in clause (i). Write
$A_j:=\theta_j((a_1^{(j)},a_2^{(j)}))$ for its image and
$b_j:=\theta_j^{-1}$ and
$q_j(\theta):=b_j(\theta)|b_j'(\theta)|/\sin\theta$ for its branch density
from clause (i), defined on $A_j$.
Angular images are not required to be disjoint. The **differential
cross-section of the model for this family** is, for
$\theta\in A:=\bigcup_{j=1}^N A_j$,
$$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma_{\mathcal B}}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta) :=\sum_{\{j:\,\theta\in A_j\}}q_j(\theta).$$
Thus $q_j$ is the contribution of branch $j$, and contributions add at every
angle belonging to more than one image. The total density for this family is
left undefined at angles belonging to no branch image. No claim is made that
the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$ or that the family includes every
deflection of the model.

**(iii) Cross-section measure and truncated totals.** For one branch $j$ with image $A_j$, and a Borel angular window $Y\subseteq A_j$, define
$$\sigma_j(Y):=\int_Yq_j(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,d\lambda_1(\theta)=\int_{Y\times(0,2\pi)}b_j(\theta)|b_j'(\theta)|\,d\lambda_2.$$
When only one branch is under discussion, write $\sigma(Y)$ for this
branch-specific measure.
For the finite family $\mathcal B$ of clause (ii), define
$$\sigma_{\mathcal B}(Y):=\sum_{j=1}^N\sigma_j(Y\cap A_j)=\int_{Y\cap A}\frac{\mathrm d\sigma_{\mathcal B}}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,d\lambda_1(\theta)$$
for every Borel $Y\subseteq(0,\pi)$. These are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over measurable sets in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], with extended value $+\infty$ allowed. The measure-level identity of [[thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density]] identifies each branch integral with the area of that branch's incident preimage; finite additivity gives the family formula, including where angular images overlap. On a compact interior interval each branch integral equals the ordinary Riemann integral; on an open interval its value is the monotone limit over compact interior truncations, equivalently the nonnegative improper integral when finite. General Borel windows use the Lebesgue integral, not a two-piece interval improper integral.
The **ideal total cross-section** of a branch is $\sigma_j(A_j)$; for a family it is $\sigma_{\mathcal B}(A)$. If infinite, there is no finite ideal total. Every compact interior angular window in a branch image has finite branch cross-section; more generally a cutoff whose incident preimage is bounded has finite cross-section. An arbitrary positive angular cutoff need not suffice for an arbitrary branch.

**(iv) The uniform-incident reading.** Under the uniform-incident preparation
of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv) with cutoff $b_{\max}$ and flux
$\Phi$, the model predicts the expected rate of scattered labels into a
Borel angular window $Y$ from one branch to be the flux times its cutoff
cross-section for the portion of that branch with $b<b_{\max}$. Writing
$T_j(b,\varphi)=(\theta_j(b),\varphi)$ on the branch rectangle and
$D_{\max}=(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi)$, the branch cutoff measure is
$$\sigma_{j,b_{\max}}(Y):=\nu\!\left(T_j^{-1}(Y\times(0,2\pi))\cap ((a_1^{(j)},a_2^{(j)})\times(0,2\pi))\cap D_{\max}\right),$$
and its expected rate is $\Phi\sigma_{j,b_{\max}}(Y)$. For a finite family
with pairwise disjoint incident intervals, define
$\sigma_{\mathcal B,b_{\max}}(Y):=\sum_{j=1}^N\sigma_{j,b_{\max}}(Y)$;
the expected rate is $\Phi\sigma_{\mathcal B,b_{\max}}(Y)$, including when
the angular images overlap. If the entire incident preimage of $Y$ lies
below the cutoff, this sum is $\Phi\sigma_{\mathcal B}(Y)$. This is a
prediction of the model under the adopted preparation. In particular:

- $\sigma_j(Y)$ and $\sigma_{\mathcal B}(Y)$ are **not** probabilities per
  incident label, **not** counts of detected events, and **not** apparatus
  properties;
- a comparison with data requires a separately specified experiment: an
  apparatus model, a detector with finite angular resolution and acceptance,
  a sampling model and uncertainties, and a statistical analysis, none of
  which is supplied by this page;
- an ideal branch cross-section may diverge at a forward angle, while
  the adopted finite incident cutoff gives
  $\sigma_{\mathcal B,b_{\max}}(Y)\le\pi b_{\max}^{2}$ for every
  window $Y$, because the branch incident intervals are disjoint. Thus
  these cutoff rates are finite even if the ideal window cross-section
  is infinite. Without an incident cutoff, the rate $\Phi\sigma_{\mathcal B}(Y)$
  is finite exactly when that ideal window cross-section is finite.
  A finite measured rate constrains the model jointly with its incident
  preparation and apparatus acceptance;
- finite samples fluctuate: an observed angular distribution can miss a
  branch's features with positive probability under ordinary sampling models,
  and agreement is evidence about the model-plus-apparatus assumptions, not a
  proof of the model.

**(v) Status and exclusions.** The branch hypothesis includes
$\theta'\ne0$: the definition excludes angles at which
$\theta'(b)=0$ (rainbow-type stationary deflections) and leaves them to
separate limiting measures. It also excludes, at the level of this page,
friction and tangential contact laws, attractive capture, screening,
radiation, relativistic and quantum modifications, and any identification of
the model parameters with measured electromagnetic quantities; those require
separate models or cross-framework items. The functions $\theta$, $b$ and the
data $E$, $J$, $u$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model data
([[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (vi)).

**Why the objects are defined.** The inverse $b$ is $C^1$ with
$b'(\theta)=1/\theta'(b(\theta))$ because a $C^1$ function on an interval with
nowhere vanishing derivative is strictly monotone and has a differentiable
inverse ([[def-cm-scattering-data]]); $\sin\theta>0$ on $(0,\pi)$; hence the
denominators do not vanish and the density is finite at every interior point
of the branch image. The pushforward identity that justifies the reading
"density carried by the branch" is
[[thm-cm-differential-cross-section-density]], a theorem of this page's
mathematical suppliers.

items.title: Finite-range central scattering in the model class: the scattering motion on all of time, the asymptotic velocities and impact parameter $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$, the advance $\Delta$ with principal deflection $\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$, and the cross-section of a deflection branch
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for clause 4 and its preparation measures.

Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, static
central pair potential $u\in C^2((0,\infty))$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $E>0$, $J>0$; write
$$V(r):=u(r)+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Suppose:

**(H1) finite range:** there is $R>0$ with $u(r)=0$ for every $r\ge R$;

**(H2) simple outer turning point:** there is $r_*>0$ with
$$V(r_*)=E,\qquad V'(r_*)<0,\qquad V(r)<E\quad(r>r_*).$$

Let $r:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model
on an interval $I$ with nonempty interior and with attached angular
momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ and attached energy $E$
([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]), and suppose
$|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for every $t\in I$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some
$t_*\in I$. Then:

1. **(The scattering motion.)** $r$ extends uniquely to a central-force
   trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ for $(\mu,u)$; the extension is
   the relative coordinate of a motion of the two-label model with its autonomous force law extended to time window $\mathbb R$, defined on all
   of $\mathbb R$, whose centre of mass is the affine extension of the
   original one. Along $\bar r$, $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies $\rho\ge r_*$,
   $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$ is strictly decreasing on
   $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on $[t_*,\infty)$; no collision
   occurs. Moreover the time quadrature
   $$\tau(r_0):=\int_{r_*}^{r_0}\frac{\mathrm ds}{\sqrt{(2/\mu)\bigl(E-V(s)\bigr)}}\qquad(r_0\ge r_*)$$
   with the integral at $r_*$ interpreted as an improper integral, is finite
   for every $r_0$ and satisfies $\rho(t_*\pm\tau(r_0))=r_0$.
2. **(Free asymptotes, speed and impact parameter.)** The limits
   $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\bar r'(t)$ exist and
   $$|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty .$$
   For every $t_1\ge t_*$ with $\rho(t_1)\ge R$ the motion is exactly free
   from $t_1$ on, $\bar r(t)=\bar r(t_1)+(t-t_1)v_+$ for all $t\ge t_1$;
   symmetrically for the incoming branch with $v_-$. The perpendicular
   distance from the force centre of the affine extensions of the incoming and outgoing free tails is the same number
   $$b=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}},\qquad\text{so that}\qquad J=\mu b\,v_\infty .$$
3. **(Polar advance and deflection.)** Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data of
   $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ from clause 1 in an oriented orthonormal triad with $e_3=j/J$
   ([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]). Then
   $$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty) =\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{J\,\mathrm dr}{r^2\sqrt{2\mu\,\bigl(E-V(r)\bigr)}}$$
   is finite and positive, and the asymptotic directions satisfy
   $$\frac{v_+}{|v_+|}=-R_{2\Delta}\Bigl(\frac{v_-}{|v_-|}\Bigr),\qquad \frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{|v_-|\,|v_+|}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta),$$
   where for $x\in\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)$,
   $R_\alpha x:=\cos\alpha\,x+\sin\alpha\,(e_3\times x)$ is the rotation of
   that plane by $\alpha$. The scattering angle of the
   motion is $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$; if
   $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ then $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi)$ and the
   signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi$.
4. **(Cross-section of a deflection branch.)** Let
   $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a deflection branch of the model in the
   sense of [[def-cm15-cross-section]]: $\theta$ is $C^1$ with
   $\theta'(b)\ne0$, and for every $b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of
   the model with impact parameter $b$, fixed energy $E$ and angular momentum magnitude
   $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$ has scattering angle $\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)=\theta(b)$, with
   $0<\Delta(b)<\pi/2$. For each member of this family suppose (H2) and the trajectory hypotheses hold with its own $J(b)$ and turning point $r_*(b)$. Then, for every nonnegative Borel test function on the branch image, or real Borel test function absolutely integrable for its outgoing measure,
   $$\int_{(a_1,a_2)\times(0,2\pi)}g(\theta(b),\varphi)b\,d\lambda_2(b,\varphi)=\int_{(\theta_1,\theta_2)\times(0,2\pi)}g(\theta,\varphi)b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|\,d\lambda_2(\theta,\varphi),$$
   the outgoing angular measure of the branch has density
   $b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|$ with respect to $\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi$,
   and the differential cross-section of the branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta) =\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'(b(\theta))\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2).$$
   Under the uniform-incident preparation of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv), with cutoff $b_{\max}>a_1$ and flux $\Phi$, put $c=\min(a_2,b_{\max})$ and
   $$Y=\theta((a_1,c)),\qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{br}}(Y)=\int_Y\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,d\lambda_1(\theta).$$
   Here $\sigma_{\mathrm{br}}(Y)$ is this branch's contribution as in clause (iii) of [[def-cm15-cross-section]], not the total model cross-section when other branch images overlap $Y$. The window uses the image of the open interval, with one-sided endpoint limits when necessary, and works for either monotonicity. The expected scattered rate from this branch portion is $\Phi\sigma_{\mathrm{br}}(Y)=\Phi\pi(c^2-a_1^2)$, which is finite. Other branch portions, if present, add their own contributions.
5. **(Scope of the statement.)** The theorem asserts nothing about the
   deflection map outside the recorded branch: it neither asserts that
   $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}$ is decreasing, injective or free of
   stationary points, nor that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$; and it
   treats finite-range potentials only. The collisions, long-range
   potentials, velocity-dependent forces and external forces are excluded by
   the model class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] and by (H1).
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: transfer the model data to the finite-range scattering theory of the mathematical suppliers, reconstruct the model motion from the affine centre of mass and the global trajectory, and read off the asymptotic velocities, impact parameter, polar advance, deflection relation and branch cross-section.
items.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the branch and preparation measures, the scattering prediction of the restricted two-label central model class with a finite-range $C^2$ potential and a simple outer turning point: the relative motion lives on all of time with one apsis and two monotone branches; the asymptotic velocities exist with speed $\sqrt{2E/\mu}$; at and beyond the range the branches are exactly free and the incoming and outgoing lines have perpendicular distance $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$; the half-angle advance is the stated quadrature and the asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle $\pi-2\Delta$ when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$; and on a $C^1$ deflection branch that records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure has the branch contribution density $b|\mathrm db/\mathrm d\theta|/\sin\theta$ and the expected uniform-incident rate is the flux times that branch's truncated cross-section. A finite family's total density adds its branch contributions where angular images overlap. The result is a conditional deduction inside the adopted model class; it uses the model data $E,J,u$ and no measured value, asserts no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, and reports no detection.

items.title: Repulsive Coulomb scattering in the model class: global non-colliding motion, the deflection map $\theta=2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$, the Rutherford density $(\kappa/4E)^2\csc^4(\theta/2)$, finite angular cutoffs and the divergent ideal total
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the cross-section measures.

Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu$, and the **repulsive Coulomb
potential**
$$u(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}\qquad(r>0),\qquad \kappa>0,$$
where $\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model
([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\kappa]=\mathsf M\ell^3\tau^{-2}$), so that
$$V(r)=\frac{\kappa}{r}+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Let the data satisfy $E>0$, $J>0$ and put
$$b:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}}>0,\qquad \alpha:=\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}>0.$$
Then:

1. **(Turning data.)** $V$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, with
   $V(r)\to+\infty$ as $r\downarrow0$ and $V(r)\to0$ as $r\to\infty$; the
   equation $V(r)=E$ has exactly one solution $r_*>0$, it is simple
   ($V'(r_*)<0$), one has $V(r)<E$ for every $r>r_*$ and $V(r)>E$ for every
   $0<r<r_*$, and $V=U^{\mathrm{eff}}_J$ is of class $C^2$ with no other
   crossing of the level $E$.
2. **(Global non-colliding scattering motion.)** Let $I\subseteq I_0$ be a time interval with nonempty interior and $r:I\to\mathbb R^3$
   be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model with attached angular
   momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3$ and energy $E$, with $|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for
   every $t\in I$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some $t_*\in I$. Then $r$
   extends uniquely to a central-force trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to
   \mathbb R^3$ whose extension is the relative coordinate of a motion of
   the two-label model with its autonomous force law extended to time window $\mathbb R$; $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies
   $\rho\ge r_*>0$ (no collision), $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$
   is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on
   $[t_*,\infty)$; the asymptotic velocities $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}
   \bar r'(t)$ exist with
   $|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty$, and the asymptotic perpendicular
   distance of each branch to its limiting direction equals
   $b=J/(\mu v_\infty)=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$, so that $J=\mu b\,v_\infty$. Unlike
   the finite-range case, there is no radius beyond which the motion is
   exactly free: the limits above are asymptotic.
3. **(Deflection and its single branch.)** With polar data $(\rho,\theta)$ in
   a triad with $e_3=j/J$, the half-angle of the motion is
   $$\Delta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr),$$
   its scattering angle is
   $$\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb}\in(0,\pi),$$
   and its signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi=-2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$.
   For the family at fixed $\mu,\kappa,E$ and varying $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$, realised by the apsis initial data of [[thm-cm-coulomb-scattering]] clause 4, the **deflection map**
   $$\theta_{\mathrm{def}}:(0,\infty)\to(0,\pi),\qquad \theta_{\mathrm{def}}(b):=2\arctan\frac{\kappa}{2Eb},$$
   is $C^1$ and strictly decreasing, hence a $C^1$ bijection with inverse
   $b(\theta)=\dfrac{\kappa}{2E}\cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}$; it is a single
   deflection branch of the model on $(0,\infty)$ with
   $\theta_{\mathrm{def}}'(b)\ne0$ everywhere and no wrapping
   ($0<\Delta<\pi/2$ for every $b>0$).
4. **(Cross-section, angular cutoffs and divergence.)** The differential
   cross-section of that branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)=\Bigl(\frac{\kappa}{4E}\Bigr)^2\csc^4\frac{\theta}{2}\qquad(0<\theta<\pi),$$
   finite and positive; for $0<\theta_1<\theta_2<\pi$ the truncated total
   cross-section over the angular band is the finite number
   $$\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\theta_2)\bigr) =\pi\bigl(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2\bigr),$$
   and by monotonicity the band $\theta\ge\theta_1$ has
   $\sigma\bigl((\theta_1,\pi)\bigr)=\pi b(\theta_1)^2 =\pi\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{2E}\bigr)^2\cot^2\frac{\theta_1}{2}$; whereas the
   truncated integral over $(0,\theta_0)$ diverges for every
   $\theta_0\in(0,\pi)$, so the **model has no finite ideal total cross-section**. Every positive angular cutoff therefore yields a finite
   truncated cross-section, and the model is predictive only jointly with an
   angular acceptance.
5. **(Status of the parameter and exclusions.)** The coupling $\kappa$ is a
   parameter of the mechanical model. This item does not identify it with
   $q_1q_2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ or with any electromagnetic quantity, states
   no measured value, and asserts no screening law for a medium of
   scatterers. Attractive Coulomb scattering (for which capture is possible
   for suitable data), inelastic, radiative, relativistic and quantum
   modifications are outside the adopted model and this statement.
items.strategy: A Coulomb specialisation: verify the turning-point hypotheses from the strict monotonicity of the effective potential, apply the Coulomb scattering theorem to the model motion, identify the deflection map and its inverse, and evaluate the band cross-sections and the divergence by the fundamental theorem.
items.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for cross-section measures, the separate long-range Coulomb scattering theorem, as a model prediction: the repulsive $\kappa/r$ potential has a unique simple outer turning point and every relative motion of the stated data extends to all of time without collision, with asymptotic velocities of speed $\sqrt{2E/\mu}$ and asymptotic impact distance $b=J/\sqrt{2\mu E}$; the deflection map is the $C^1$ decreasing bijection $2\arctan(\kappa/(2Eb))$ with a single branch, the differential cross-section is the Rutherford density $(\kappa/4E)^2\csc^4(\theta/2)$, every angular band has the finite truncated cross-section $\pi(b(\theta_1)^2-b(\theta_2)^2)$, and the ideal total cross-section diverges at forward angles. The parameter $\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model and is not identified with any electromagnetic quantity; the result reports no measurement, no screening law and no capture, radiation, relativistic or quantum modification.

items.title: Adopted impact and open-mass extensions of the force branch: the isolated reciprocal impulse model, the collinear restitution contact law and the open-body material accounting
items.statement:
Adopt, as this page's **impact and open-mass extensions** of the force
branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the following three model extensions. Each is an adopted model, not a
consequence of the smooth-force postulates; each applies only where a
statement explicitly invokes it.

**(i) The isolated reciprocal impulse model.** A two-label force model with
masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), time window $I_0$,
configuration domain $Q$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]) and continuous
external-plus-pair force maps $F_1,F_2$ is **run in the isolated reciprocal
impulse model at $t_*\in I_0$** when there is an interval
$I\subseteq I_0$ with $t_*\in\operatorname{int}I$ and a position curve
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ such that the following conditions hold. This curve is
called an **impulse motion**; only its restrictions away from $t_*$ are
motions of the associated first-order system of [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]],
and no differentiability at $t_*$ is required:

1. $x_1,x_2$ are continuous on $I$ and twice continuously differentiable on
   each of $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$
   ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]],
   [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and
   $m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every $t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}$;
2. the one-sided limits
   $v_i^{\pm}:=\lim_{t\to t_*\pm}x_i'(t)$ exist in $\mathbb R^3$
   ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]);
3. there is a vector $J\in\mathbb R^3$, the **impulse**, with
   $$m_1\bigl(v_1^+-v_1^-\bigr)=J,\qquad m_2\bigl(v_2^+-v_2^-\bigr)=-J .$$

The two equations of clause 3 are the **reciprocal finite-jump form** of the
isolated impulse: the two labels receive equal and opposite momentum changes.
The regular force maps remain continuous on their state domain; their
evaluations along the curve can have different one-sided limits because the
velocity can jump. The dimension of the impulse
is $[J]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

For the distributional rendering on $\operatorname{int}I$, assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Put
$p_i(t)=m_ix_i'(t)$ and $f_i(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$ off $t_*$, assigning both
the value $0$ at $t_*$. Their one-sided limits are finite: those of $p_i$
are $m_iv_i^\pm$, and continuity of the state-domain force maps gives
$f_i(t_*^\pm)=F_i(t_*,x(t_*),v^\pm)$, with
$v^\pm=(v_1^\pm,v_2^\pm)$. Also $p_i'=f_i$ off the impulse. Thus each
component meets the piecewise-$C^1$ and one-sided derivative-limit
hypotheses of [[lem-cm-piecewise-c1-jump-derivative]]. Its identity,
summed componentwise, gives for every real vector test function
$\Phi\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{int}I;\mathbb R^3)$ (each component is
smooth and compactly supported, [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]])
$$-\int_{\operatorname{int}I}\langle p_i,\Phi'\rangle\,d\lambda=\int_{\operatorname{int}I}\langle f_i,\Phi\rangle\,d\lambda+s_i\langle J,\Phi(t_*)\rangle,\qquad s_1=1,\quad s_2=-1,$$
where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure and the integral convention is that of
[[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. This is the pairing form of the
adopted jumps. Unlike [[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]], whose
hypotheses require continuous time forces and assume the pairings to derive
the jumps, this rendering allows distinct one-sided regular-force values.

**(ii) The collinear restitution contact law.** A model run in the isolated
reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$ is **collinear** when there is a unit vector
$n\in\mathbb R^3$ (the **contact direction**) with $v_i^{\pm}\parallel n$ for
$i=1,2$ and $\langle v_2^--v_1^-,n\rangle<0$ (the labels approach along $n$).
For a collinear contact, adopt a **coefficient of restitution** $e\in[0,1]$ —
a dimensionless model datum of the pair and the contact — and the **restitution
law**
$$v_2^+-v_1^+=-e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
For $e=1$ the contact is called **elastic**, for $e=0$ **perfectly inelastic**
and otherwise **semi-elastic**; the law is a constitutive assumption, not a
consequence of the impulse equations of clause (i), and $e$ is not derived
from the masses or the approach speed. The law is stated only for a single
collinear contact; simultaneous contacts, repeated contacts and tangential
(friction) impulses are outside the model.

**(iii) The open-body material accounting.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a
nonempty open interval. Adopt for a body whose mass
$m:I\to(0,\infty)$ and velocity $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$ are differentiable, and
whose external force and exchanged matter are described by maps
$F:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$ and
$w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ (mass rates and *inertial*
velocities of the matter entering and leaving, measured in the same inertial
frame as $v$), the **material balance identities**
$$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad (mv)'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}} .$$
They are the mathematical rendering of "gains $r_{\mathrm{in}}\,\mathrm dt$ of
matter with velocity $w_{\mathrm{in}}$, loses $r_{\mathrm{out}}\,\mathrm dt$
with velocity $w_{\mathrm{out}}$, and feels the external force $F$", and they
are adopted rather than derived from a closed-system law. Their product-rule
consequence $mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$
is proved in [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]; in particular the
closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ is recovered only when
$r_{\mathrm{in}}w_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}w_{\mathrm{out}}$.
The quantities have types and SI dimensions
$[m]=\mu$, $[v]=[w_{\mathrm{in}}]=[w_{\mathrm{out}}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$,
$[F]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ and
$[r_{\mathrm{in}}]=[r_{\mathrm{out}}]=\mu\tau^{-1}$; they are model
data, not measured values.
items.strategy: An adopted model extension: the isolated reciprocal impulse with its finite momentum jump, the collinear restitution contact law with coefficient in [0,1], and the open-body material accounting with entering and leaving mass rates and inertial velocities, together with their status and exclusions.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the page's impact and open-mass extensions of the framework's force branch: an isolated reciprocal impulse at one time (a finite momentum jump of opposite sign for the two labels, with the regular dynamics retained away from that time), a collinear restitution contact law with coefficient $0\le e\le1$ fixing only the relative velocity, and an open-body material accounting for matter entering and leaving a body at given rates with given inertial velocities. The item adopts model extensions and names their mathematical renderings; it derives nothing from the smooth-force postulates, asserts no law of nature, no measured value for $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and excludes simultaneous contacts, friction, deformation modes and coefficients outside $[0,1]$.

items.title: Consequences of the adopted impact and open-mass models: continuity of total momentum, the smooth-force exclusion, the restitution solution with $\Delta K=-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$, and the open-body and rocket laws
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]),
inherited from the statement of
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]], whose distributional jump
lemma uses it; the algebraic clauses used here do not otherwise use choice.
Adopt the impact and open-mass extensions of [[post-cm15-impulse]], with
$m_1,m_2>0$, an interval $I$ with nonempty interior, $t_*\in\operatorname{int} I$, an impulse motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ run in the isolated reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$
with impulse $J$ and one-sided velocities $v_i^\pm$, and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\qquad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\qquad P(t):=m_1x_1'(t)+m_2x_2'(t)\qquad(t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}).$$
Only the one-sided limits of $P$ at $t_*$ are used; no derivative of the
position curves at the contact time is assumed.
Then:

1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the
   impact,
   $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$
   and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$:
   $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$.
2. **(Smooth-force exclusion.)** Suppose this same candidate motion $x$ from
   clause 1 also satisfies the smooth force branch of
   [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] on $I$,
   with the force maps continuous there. Then the momentum curves
   $p_i=m_ix_i'$ are of class $C^1$ on $I$; in particular
   $$p_i(t_*^+)=p_i(t_*^-)\qquad(i=1,2).$$
   Clause 1 identifies the jump of $p_1$ with the same impulse $J$, so
   $J=0$: no candidate motion carrying a nonzero isolated impulse can also
   be a motion of that smooth-force class. The finite-jump model of
   [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i) is therefore a genuine extension of the
   smooth-force branch, not one of its cases.
3. **(Collinear restitution solution.)** Suppose in addition that the
   contact is collinear with contact direction $n$ and coefficient of
   restitution $e\in[0,1]$ ([[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii)). Then
   $$J=\mu(1+e)\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),$$
   $J$ is parallel to $n$, the centre-of-mass velocity
   $V:=M^{-1}(m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-)$ is unchanged across the impact, and the
   post-impact velocities are
   $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
4. **(Kinetic energy of the impact.)** The kinetic-energy change across the
   impact is
   $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2} -\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2} =-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0,$$
   with equality if and only if $e=1$ or $v_2^-=v_1^-$. For $0\le e<1$ the
   contact model is dissipative: the total kinetic energy of the two labels
   is not conserved across the impact, and the deficit
   $\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ is a quantity of the
   adopted contact law. This item identifies it with no measured heat,
   temperature, sound or deformation observable.
5. **(Momentum balance alone does not determine the impact.)** In the
   collinear case with $d^-:=v_2^--v_1^-$ and $d_n:=\langle d^-,n\rangle<0$,
   the impulse equations of clause 1 alone leave the scalar impulse magnitude
   free: for every real $J_n$ with $J_n\le \mu d_n$ (so that the contact is
   separating or grazing) the velocities
   $$v_1^+=v_1^-+\frac{J_n}{m_1}n,\qquad v_2^+=v_2^--\frac{J_n}{m_2}n$$
   satisfy the reciprocal impulse equations with impulse $J=J_nn$ and
   preserve the total momentum, and their kinetic-energy change is
   $$\Delta K(J_n)=-J_n\,d_n+\frac{J_n^2}{2\mu},$$
   whose minimum over the admissible range is
   $\Delta K(\mu d_n)=-\frac{\mu}{2}d_n^2$ at the perfectly inelastic value
   $J_n=\mu d_n$ (that is, $e=0$). The value of
   $J_n$ is fixed only by the contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (ii), which selects $J_n=\mu(1+e)d_n$; in particular momentum balance
   alone does not determine the post-impact velocities.
6. **(Open-body and rocket laws.)** Under [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (iii), with differentiable $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ and $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
   $F:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$,
   and $w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the
   material balance identities, one has on $I$
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr).$$
   In particular: (a) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ then
   $m\,v'=F$ and $(mv)'=F$; (b) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ and
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'>0$ (mass loss) then
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr)=F-m'\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr),$$
   so the **thrust** is $T:=r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$,
   and the closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ fails unless
   $w_{\mathrm{out}}=0$; (c) if $r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ and $w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$
   then $m\,v'=F-r_{\mathrm{in}}v$: capture contributes the acceleration
   $-(r_{\mathrm{in}}/m)v$, opposing $v$, while $(mv)'=F$ still holds.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction from the adopted models: momentum continuity across the impulse, the smooth-force exclusion, the restitution velocities and kinetic-energy change, the underdetermination by momentum alone, and the open-body and rocket laws with their special cases.
items.physical_scope: The conditional consequences of the page's adopted impact and open-mass extensions: total momentum is continuous across an isolated reciprocal impulse with the impulse removed from the second label; a smooth-force motion with continuous force maps cannot carry a nonzero impulse, so the contact model is an extension rather than a smooth-force theorem; a collinear contact with coefficient of restitution $e\in[0,1]$ has the stated post-impact velocities and kinetic-energy change, is dissipative for $e<1$, and its contact law is an independent assumption not derivable from momentum balance; and the open-body material accounting yields the derived law $mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$ with the rocket thrust as the special case. The result is a conditional deduction from adopted model data; it asserts no measured value of $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and identifies no observed dissipation mechanism.

items.title: The finite-regularity open-flow model: moving-control-region mass and momentum balances, their material and fixed special cases, and the inlet/outlet decomposition reproducing the open-body and rocket laws
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport and divergence theorems.
**Adopt the finite-regularity open-flow model** with the following model data in one
fixed inertial frame (the adapted affine chart of [[post-cm01-frames]]) and
with SI conventions ([[def-cm01-units]]): a nonempty open interval $I$; a
material region $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ (bounded open with $C^1$ boundary);
a motion $\chi$ of $B$ on $I$ of class $C^2$ whose time slices are
diffeomorphisms with positive Jacobian onto their images. Let $U\subseteq
\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ be an open common field domain containing the
swept region over a compact subinterval $J_0$ with
$\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$. On $U$ take a scalar mass-density field
$\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ of class $C^1$ with
$[\rho]=\mu\ell^{-3}$ ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]], where
mass on a spatial region $C$ is $\int_C\rho\,dx$); its spatial velocity
field $u:U\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^1$ with $[u]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and
$u(t,\chi(t,X))=\partial_t\chi(t,X)$
([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]); a Cauchy stress matrix field
$\sigma:U\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ of class $C^1$ with
$[\sigma]=\mu\ell^{-1}\tau^{-2}$, representing the traction by
$\mathbf t(\nu)=\sigma\nu$ on a surface with unit normal $\nu$
([[def-cm-traction-and-stress]]); and a continuous specific body-force vector
$b:U\to\mathbb R^3$, meaning force per unit mass and distinct from the
material acceleration, with $[b]=\ell\tau^{-2}$.
For the material derivative used below, make the time-dependent convention
explicit:
$$D_tu(t,x):=\partial_tu(t,x)+(D_xu(t,x))u(t,x),\qquad (D_tu)_i=\partial_tu_i+\sum_{j=1}^3u_j\,\partial_{x_j}u_i,$$
where $\partial_t$ differentiates at fixed $x$ and $D_xu$ is the spatial
Jacobian at fixed $t$ ([[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]],
[[def-cm-continuum-motion]]). Define the row divergence by
$g_i:=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$, so $g$ is a vector force
density with units $\mu\ell^{-2}\tau^{-2}$. Adopt as the model's
**material balances**: for every material subregion $B'\subseteq B$ (a
nonempty bounded open subset with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$ whose images
$\chi_t(B')$ are bounded $C^1$ domains,
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]) and every
$t\in J_0$,

$$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho\,\mathrm dx=0,\qquad \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho u\,\mathrm dx=\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(B')}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS,$$

with $\nu$ the outward unit normal and the surface integral that of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. These two balance
laws are **adopted model assumptions** of this item, in the sense of the
open-body accounting of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (iii); they are not
derived from the particle postulates. Then, for every second motion $\psi$ of
a material region $B'\subseteq B$ on $I$ (the **control motion**) with
control regions $C_t:=\psi_t(B')$ that are bounded $C^1$ domains for
   $t\in J_0$, spatial velocity $w$ with $[w]=\ell\tau^{-1}$, and outward
   unit normal $\nu$.
Require its closed sweep $\Sigma_C:=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline{B'})\}$ to lie in the common open field domain. Require also either that this sweep lie locally inside the current material region $\chi_t(B)$, where localization supplies the local mass and momentum equations, or that those same local equations $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ and $\rho D_tu=\rho b+g$ be explicitly adopted on a neighbourhood of the control sweep. The control motion need not coincide with $\chi$. Then:

1. **(Control-volume identities.)** For every $t\in J_0$,
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx =-\int_{\partial C_t}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS, \tag{CV1}$$
   and componentwise
   $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_{C_t}\rho u_i\,\mathrm dx =\int_{C_t}\rho b_i\,\mathrm dx+\Bigl(\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS\Bigr)_i -\int_{\partial C_t}\rho u_i\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\qquad(i=1,2,3). \tag{CV2}$$
2. **(Material and fixed special cases.)** If $\psi=\chi$ (the control region
   is material, $w=u$ on the boundary), the flux terms vanish and (CV1),
   (CV2) reduce to the adopted material balances; if $\psi$ is the constant
   motion ($w=0$, $C_t=C$ fixed), then
   $$m_C'=-\int_{\partial C}\rho\,u\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS,\qquad P_C'=\int_C\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS-\int_{\partial C}\rho u\,(u\cdot\nu)\,\mathrm dS$$
   with $m_C:=\int_C\rho$, $P_C:=\int_C\rho u$; the last term is the momentum
   flux through the fixed boundary, and the relation is the fixed-region
   steady-flow balance of the engineering treatment when the fields are
   steady and the region fixed.
3. **(Inlet/outlet decomposition and the open-body law.)** Suppose that for
   every $t\in J_0$ the boundary decomposes into finitely many $C^1$ pieces,
   among which $\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu<0$),
   $\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}$ (where $(u-w)\cdot\nu>0$) and the zero-flux rest,
   and put
   $$r_{\mathrm{in}}:=-\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{out}}:=\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,\mathrm dS\ge0,$$
   $$w_{\mathrm{in}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{in}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{in},t}}\rho u\,\bigl(-(u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS,\qquad w_{\mathrm{out}}:=\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{out}}}\int_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{out},t}}\rho u\,\bigl((u-w)\cdot\nu\bigr)\mathrm dS$$
   (the flux averages are used only where the corresponding rate is
   positive; define $r_{\mathrm{in}}w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ when
   $r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$, and likewise for the outlet term), and write
   $$m:=\int_{C_t}\rho\,\mathrm dx>0,\qquad P:=\int_{C_t}\rho u\,\mathrm dx,\qquad F_{\mathrm{ext}}:=\int_{C_t}\rho b\,\mathrm dx+\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,\mathrm dS .$$
   The units are $[m]=\mu$, $[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$,
   $[F_{\mathrm{ext}}]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$,
   $[r_{\mathrm{in}}]=[r_{\mathrm{out}}]=\mu\tau^{-1}$ and
   $[w_{\mathrm{in}}]=[w_{\mathrm{out}}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$. The control-volume
   theorem supplies the derivatives of $m$ and $P$; since $\rho>0$ and each
   $C_t$ is a nonempty open region, $m>0$, so $v:=P/m$ is differentiable on
   $J_0$. This verifies the differentiability hypotheses of
   [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]].
   Then the control-volume identities read
   $$m'=r_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}},\qquad P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\,w_{\mathrm{in}}-r_{\mathrm{out}}\,w_{\mathrm{out}},$$
   and the lumped body with mass $m$ and velocity $v:=P/m$ satisfies
   $$m\,v'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr),$$
   the derived law of [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]]. In
   particular, a body that only loses mass ($r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$,
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'$) has thrust
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$, and a body
   whose boundary moves with the material ($w=u$; no flux) has
   $m'=0$ and $P'=F_{\mathrm{ext}}$.
4. **(Status.)** The balances displayed before clause 1 are adopted component
   models of the open flow, exactly as clause (iii) of
   [[post-cm15-impulse]] adopts the lumped accounting; this item proves only
   the two stated deductions (localization followed by the control-volume
   identities, and the inlet/outlet reading). It asserts no constitutive law
   for $\rho$ or $\sigma$, no boundary condition, no incompressibility, no
   regularity beyond that stated, and no empirical claim; the fields,
   the control motion and the region are model data.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the scattering measures.

This remark records the boundaries of the page's claims. It adds no
statement of its own and no empirical content; each clause refers to the
items that do.

## What the scattering items assert

[[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]] is a conditional deduction inside the
two-label central model class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with a
finite-range $C^2$ potential and a simple outer turning point: the relative
motion extends to all of time, its asymptotic velocities and impact
parameter are computed, the half-angle advance is a quadrature, the
asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle
$\pi-2\Delta$ when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$, and on a smooth deflection branch that
records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure has that
branch's cross-section contribution $b|b'|/\sin\theta$.
[[def-cm15-cross-section]] sums contributions from disjoint incident
intervals, including where their angular images overlap.
[[pthm-cm15-rutherford-model]]
treats the separate long-range repulsive $\kappa/r$ potential and adds the explicit
deflection map, the Rutherford density, the finite truncated band values and
the divergence of the ideal total.

## What the scattering items do not assert

- **No monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map.**
  [[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]] clause 5 states explicitly that the map
  $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}$ is not asserted to be decreasing, injective or
  free of stationary points, and that the branch images are not asserted to
  cover $(0,\pi)$. The counterexample
  [[cex-cm15-deflection-need-not-decrease]] shows that global strict decrease
  fails even in the smooth finite-range class because the deflection has a
  constant free tail; its separate adopted contact comparison also has an
  increasing branch. The cross-section formula of
  [[def-cm15-cross-section]] therefore applies to specified invertible
  branches rather than assuming a global inverse.
  For a finite family of branches with disjoint incident intervals, the
  total density at an angle is the sum of all branch contributions whose
  images contain that angle; this total is distinct from any one branch's
  density.

- **Cross-section and probability are distinct.** The cross-section is a
  model quantity of the adopted uniform-incident preparation
  ([[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv),
  [[def-cm15-cross-section]] clause (iv)): it is not a count of detected
  events, not a probability per incident label, and not a property of any
  apparatus. For a specified branch and Borel angle window, the probability
  per incident label of an impact parameter in that branch's preimage is its
  incident preimage area within $D_{\max}=(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi)$ divided by $\pi b_{\max}^2$, with fixed energy and
  $J(b)=\sqrt{2\mu E}\,b$; this statement covers only the recorded branch
  portions. No experiment is authored on this page, and no measured rate,
  uncertainty or statistical claim about nature is made here. A comparison
  would require a specified apparatus, sampling model and analysis, as
  [[rem-cm05-collision-scope]] requires of the collision claims of the
  preceding page.

- **Contact scattering uses separate example rules.** The hard-sphere and
  refracting-shell models of the examples page adopt their fixed-wall and
  interface rules locally; neither full rule is supplied by
  [[post-cm15-impulse]], whose restitution law covers a finite-mass collinear
  two-label contact. These contact trajectories are not instances of the
  $C^2$ finite-range hypothesis of [[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]]. In
  particular the finite total cross-section $\pi a^2$ of the hard-sphere
  contact model is computed from its locally defined uniform incident-area
  pushforward under the separately adopted reflection rule and
  does not contradict the forward divergence of the ideal Coulomb branch.

- **No electromagnetic, screening, radiative or quantum content.** The
  Coulomb item treats $\kappa$ as a parameter of the mechanical model and
  does not identify it with $q_1q_2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ or any other
  electromagnetic quantity; it asserts no screening law for a medium of
  scatterers, no inelastic or radiative loss, and no relativistic or
  quantum modification. Attractive Coulomb capture, for which suitable data
  do allow capture, lies outside its statement.

- **Relative data do not give label angles.** The scattering angles and
  cross-section densities are computed from the reduced relative coordinate
  and its asymptotic velocities, as defined by
  [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]]. The two-label reconstruction
  $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$, $x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ shows that individual-label
  directions generally differ from the relative direction and from each
  other; this page asserts no individual-label angle.

## What the impact and open-flow items assert and adopt

[[post-cm15-impulse]] adopts three extensions of the force branch: the
isolated reciprocal impulse, the collinear restitution contact law with
$e\in[0,1]$, and the open-body material accounting.
[[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]] proves their conditional consequences —
momentum continuity across the impulse, exclusion of a nonzero impulse for a
candidate motion that also satisfies the smooth-force branch, the
restitution velocities, the kinetic-energy change and the open-body and
rocket laws — and records that momentum balance alone does not fix the
outcome. [[pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance]] derives the
moving-control-region identities from adopted material balances and
identifies the lumped accounting of the impact postulate as their
inlet/outlet specialisation.

These items assert no law of nature and no measured value: $e$, the impulse,
the contact direction and the mass rates and velocities are model data
([[def-cm01-units]] for the dimensions). They exclude contacts outside
$0\le e\le1$, simultaneous or tangential contacts, friction, rotation and
deformation modes, and — for the open flow — constitutive laws, boundary
conditions and incompressibility, which are separate models. Their empirical
reading (for instance that a particular pair of bodies has a particular
coefficient) requires a separately specified experiment, sampling model and
uncertainty analysis, and obtains evidence about the model-plus-apparatus
assumptions rather than a proof of the model.

items.title: Elastic reflection from a fixed sphere: the branch $b=a\cos(\theta/2)$, the uniform density $a^2/4$ and the total $\pi a^2$ of a contact model
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the mathematical incident and solid-angle measures below.

**Declared model.** Fix a length $a>0$ (the sphere radius) and a reduced mass
$\mu>0$. In a fixed inertial chart ([[post-cm01-frames]]), let the sphere
$S_a:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2=a\}$ be immovable and centred at the
origin. For $b\in(0,a)$ the label position is a continuous curve
$\gamma_b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$, affine on each side of one contact time
$t_*$, with one-sided velocity limits and
$P:=\gamma_b(t_*)\in S_a$. Its incoming affine line has speed
$v_\infty>0$, direction $\hat u$ and perpendicular distance $b$ from the
origin. Separately adopt, for this fixed-wall model, the **elastic reflection
rule** at the contact point with outward unit normal $n:=P/a$:
$$v^+=v^--2\langle v^-,n\rangle n,$$
that is, the normal component reverses and the tangential component is
unchanged. Its normal-velocity reversal is analogous to the $e=1$ case of
[[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii), but it is not a formal member of that law:
the postulate assumes a finite-mass two-label collinear contact, whereas this
example prescribes an immovable wall and a vector reflection rule. The inward
unit normal $-n$ makes the angle
$$\alpha:=\arcsin\frac{b}{a}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\Bigr)$$
with $\hat u$; equivalently $b=a\sin\alpha$ is the perpendicular distance of
the incoming line from the centre.

**Incident preparation and contact cross-section.** Choose orthonormal
vectors $e_1,e_2$ perpendicular to the common incoming direction $\hat u$.
For an incident offset $b e_\varphi$, where
$e_\varphi=\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\varphi\,e_2$, the first contact is
$P=b e_\varphi-\sqrt{a^2-b^2}\,\hat u$. The transverse component of the
reflected direction is a positive multiple of $e_\varphi$, so its outgoing
azimuth is $\varphi$. Let $D=(0,a)\times(0,2\pi)$ and
$Y=(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)$. Adopt uniform incident area measure
$\nu(B)=\int_B b\,d\lambda_2(b,\varphi)$ on Borel subsets of $D$ and
solid-angle measure $\Omega(B)=\int_B\sin\theta\,d\lambda_2(\theta,\varphi)$
on $Y$, using the abstract mathematical measures of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. Define the **contact cross-section measure**
by $\sigma(B):=\nu(T^{-1}(B))$, where
$T(b,\varphi)=(\theta(b),\varphi)$ is the outgoing direction map.
For an angular band $A\subseteq(0,\pi)$ abbreviate
$\sigma(A):=\sigma(A\times(0,2\pi))$.
A differential contact cross-section is a density $f$ satisfying
$\sigma(B)=\int_B f\,d\Omega$ for every Borel $B\subseteq Y$.
This is a local definition for the fixed-wall contact model, independent
of the smooth central-model class of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]].
The centre, grazing circle and azimuth seam have zero incident area and
supply no atoms; free incoming lines with $b>a$ do not hit the sphere and
are excluded from this contact cross-section.

**Assertion to check.** The motion is a single reflection with deflection
$$\theta(b)=\pi-2\alpha=\pi-2\arcsin\frac{b}{a}\in(0,\pi),$$
so the branch is $b(\theta)=a\cos(\theta/2)$ on $0<\theta<\pi$, the
differential cross-section is the constant $a^2/4$, and the truncated total
cross-section over the whole branch is $\pi a^2$.

items.physical_scope: Assuming countable choice for the locally defined incident and solid-angle measures, a separately adopted fixed-wall contact model of a reduced label of mass $\mu$ reflecting elastically from an impenetrable sphere of radius $a$: the example-specific rule reverses the normal velocity component and preserves the tangential component, so speed and angular momentum are conserved across contact. The example computes the branch contribution $b=a\cos(\theta/2)$, the constant density $a^2/4$ and the total $\pi a^2$. This fixed-wall rule is outside both the $C^2$ finite-range hypothesis of the central-scattering theorem and the finite-mass two-label restitution postulate; the $e=1$ comparison concerns only the normal-velocity reversal. The finite total does not contradict the Coulomb forward divergence. The data are declared model data; the example reports no observation or measured value.
